newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis posts 96 sales increase. [CORRECTED 16:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Novartis posts 96 sales increase. [CORRECTED 16:20 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects to delete percentage reference in headline.)

Swiss pharmaceuticals group Novartis AG, formed in December through the merger of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz AG, said sales in its core life sciences segment rose by eight percent in 1996 and that it expected to post a flat full-year profit, excluding extraordinary items. (Corrects to make clear that eight percent sales rise refers to core life sciences business which will remain after planned spinoff of specialty chemicals business and not to whole group.)
Group sales for 1996 totalled 36.23 billion Swiss francs ($25.3 billion) compared with 35.94 billion for 1995. The two companies had a combined net profit in 1995 of 4.2 billion francs.

"Excluding one-off merger-related exceptional income and expenses, Novartis expects net income for the year as a whole to be approximately at the sale level as in the previous year...," Novartis said in a statement.
The group expects to publish its 1996 financial statements on March 18.

Separately, the group said preparation for its scheduled spin-off of its Ciba Specialty Chemicals division are proceeding according to plan and that it expected to list the chemicals unit on the Swiss stock exchange before the Novartis annual general meeting on April 22. ($ = 1.434 Swiss Francs)
